case_title: Ajitsingh Harnam Singh Gujral v. State of Maharashtra
aggravating_circumstances: Pre-planned murder, use of petrol to burn victims, cruelty, barbaric manner
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to death
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married and had one son aged about 20 years and two daughters aged 22 years and 13 years respectively, killed his wife and three children by pouring petrol on their persons and setting them on fire. The incident occurred 25-27 years after the marriage. The accused was last seen with his wife at about midnight and was in fact quarreling with her at that time. The incident happened at 4 or 4.30 a.m., with a time gap of about 4 hours between the last seen time and the incident. The accused was found with cash of Rs.7,68,080/- and several items of clothing, but his alibi was deemed false. A 10-litre white plastic can with petrol was found at the scene, indicating the accused had brought petrol to the scene. The accused was found with a red bucket used for pouring petrol on the victims, which was confirmed by a chemical analysis. The prosecution's case relied on circumstantial evidence, including the presence of the accused at the scene, the petrol can, and the absence of any other plausible explanation for the crime.
